subject: math
cluster: Understand congruence and similarity using physical models, transparencies, or geometry software
intro: These problems chain together several angle facts at once: the triangle angle-sum theorem, the exterior-angle theorem, the angle pairs formed when a transversal crosses parallel lines, and the angle-angle (AA) similarity criterion. Most require three or more linked steps, an equation that needs distribution, or a short justification of which relationship you used. Work in exact degree measures and name the angle relationship at each step.

items.prompt: Lines $\ell$ and $m$ are parallel and are cut by a transversal $t$. The transversal also forms one side of a triangle. An alternate interior angle of the transversal measures $63^\circ$ and serves as one angle of the triangle; a second angle of the same triangle is $58^\circ$. The exterior angle of the triangle adjacent to the third vertex is then drawn. Find the measure of that exterior angle, and name the relationship you used for each step.

steps: The alternate interior angle equals the given $63^\circ$ (alternate interior angles formed by parallel lines are congruent), so the triangle's first angle is $63^\circ$.
The third interior angle of the triangle is $180^\circ - 63^\circ - 58^\circ = 59^\circ$ (triangle angle-sum theorem).
The exterior angle adjacent to that third vertex equals the sum of the two remote interior angles: $63^\circ + 58^\circ = 121^\circ$ (exterior-angle theorem).
Check: the exterior angle and its adjacent interior angle are a linear pair, $121^\circ + 59^\circ = 180^\circ$. The exterior angle is $121^\circ$.

items.prompt: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. A pair of corresponding angles are labeled $(4x + 17)^\circ$ and $(7x - 19)^\circ$. Find $x$, then state the measure of each angle.

steps: Corresponding angles formed by parallel lines are congruent, so set the expressions equal: $4x + 17 = 7x - 19$.
Subtract $4x$ from both sides: $17 = 3x - 19$.
Add $19$ to both sides: $36 = 3x$.
Divide by $3$: $x = 12$.
Substitute back: $4(12) + 17 = 48 + 17 = 65^\circ$, and $7(12) - 19 = 84 - 19 = 65^\circ$. Both angles measure $65^\circ$.

items.prompt: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. A pair of co-interior (same-side interior) angles measure $(5x - 8)^\circ$ and $(3x + 12)^\circ$. Find $x$ and the measure of each angle.

steps: Co-interior (same-side interior) angles formed by parallel lines are supplementary, so their measures sum to $180^\circ$: $(5x - 8) + (3x + 12) = 180$.
Combine like terms: $8x + 4 = 180$.
Subtract $4$: $8x = 176$.
Divide by $8$: $x = 22$.

items.prompt: In triangle $ABC$, the angle at $A$ is $(2x + 10)^\circ$, the angle at $B$ is $(3x - 5)^\circ$, and the exterior angle at $C$ (adjacent to the interior angle at $C$) measures $(6x - 15)^\circ$. Use the exterior-angle theorem to find $x$, then find all three interior angles of the triangle.

steps: By the exterior-angle theorem, the exterior angle at $C$ equals the sum of the two remote interior angles $A$ and $B$: $(2x + 10) + (3x - 5) = 6x - 15$.
Combine like terms on the left: $5x + 5 = 6x - 15$.
Subtract $5x$ from both sides: $5 = x - 15$.
Angle $A = 2(20) + 10 = 50^\circ$; angle $B = 3(20) - 5 = 55^\circ$; the exterior angle $= 6(20) - 15 = 105^\circ$, so the interior angle $C = 180^\circ - 105^\circ = 75^\circ$.
Check the angle sum: $50^\circ + 55^\circ + 75^\circ = 180^\circ$.

items.prompt: Triangle $ABC$ has angles $A = 38^\circ$ and $B = 67^\circ$. Triangle $DEF$ has angles $D = 75^\circ$ and $E = 67^\circ$. Determine whether the two triangles are similar. Justify your answer with the AA criterion, and if they are similar, state the correspondence of all three pairs of angles.
items.answer: Yes, the triangles are similar by AA; $A \leftrightarrow F = 38^\circ$, $B \leftrightarrow E = 67^\circ$, $C \leftrightarrow D = 75^\circ$

steps: Find the third angle of each triangle using the angle-sum theorem.
In triangle $ABC$: $C = 180^\circ - 38^\circ - 67^\circ = 75^\circ$.
In triangle $DEF$: $F = 180^\circ - 75^\circ - 67^\circ = 38^\circ$.
Both triangles have the angle set $\{38^\circ, 67^\circ, 75^\circ\}$, so at least two pairs of angles are congruent. By the AA criterion, the triangles are similar.
Matching equal angles gives the correspondence $A \leftrightarrow F$ ($38^\circ$), $B \leftrightarrow E$ ($67^\circ$), and $C \leftrightarrow D$ ($75^\circ$).

items.prompt: A transversal crosses two parallel lines. At the upper intersection an angle of $(8x - 6)^\circ$ is marked, and at the lower intersection its alternate exterior angle is marked $(5x + 21)^\circ$. Find $x$ and the common measure of the two alternate exterior angles.

steps: Alternate exterior angles formed by parallel lines cut by a transversal are congruent, so $8x - 6 = 5x + 21$.
Subtract $5x$ from both sides: $3x - 6 = 21$.
Divide by $3$: $x = 9$.
Substitute: $8(9) - 6 = 72 - 6 = 66^\circ$ and $5(9) + 21 = 45 + 21 = 66^\circ$. Each alternate exterior angle measures $66^\circ$.

items.prompt: Line segment $DE$ is drawn inside triangle $ABC$ so that $DE$ is parallel to side $BC$, with $D$ on $AB$ and $E$ on $AC$. Angle $A = 54^\circ$ and angle $B = 71^\circ$. Use parallel-line angle relationships to show that triangle $ADE$ is similar to triangle $ABC$, and find angle $AED$.
items.answer: The triangles are similar by AA; angle $AED = 55^\circ$

steps: Angle $A$ is shared by both triangle $ADE$ and triangle $ABC$, giving one pair of congruent angles ($54^\circ$ each).
Because $DE \parallel BC$ and $AB$ is a transversal, angle $ADE$ and angle $ABC$ are corresponding angles, so they are congruent: angle $ADE = 71^\circ$.
With two pairs of congruent angles (the shared angle $A$ and the corresponding angles $ADE \cong ABC$), triangle $ADE \sim$ triangle $ABC$ by AA.
In triangle $ADE$, angle $AED = 180^\circ - 54^\circ - 71^\circ = 55^\circ$ (triangle angle-sum theorem).
Check: angle $AED$ corresponds to angle $ACB = 180^\circ - 54^\circ - 71^\circ = 55^\circ$, consistent with the similarity.

items.prompt: In triangle $PQR$, the angle at $P$ is $(x + 24)^\circ$, the angle at $Q$ is $(2x)^\circ$, and the angle at $R$ is $(3x - 12)^\circ$. Find $x$, find all three angles, and state which angle is the largest.
items.answer: $x = 28$; the angles are $P = 52^\circ$, $Q = 56^\circ$, $R = 72^\circ$; angle $R$ is largest

steps: By the triangle angle-sum theorem, the three interior angles sum to $180^\circ$: $(x + 24) + 2x + (3x - 12) = 180$.
Combine like terms: $6x + 12 = 180$.
Subtract $12$: $6x = 168$.
Divide by $6$: $x = 28$.
Check: $52^\circ + 56^\circ + 72^\circ = 180^\circ$. The largest angle is $R = 72^\circ$.

items.prompt: A transversal crosses two parallel lines $\ell$ and $m$. At line $\ell$ a triangle is formed whose vertex angle on $\ell$ equals the co-interior (same-side interior) angle of a $124^\circ$ angle marked at line $m$. The second angle of this triangle is $46^\circ$. Find the third angle of the triangle, naming each relationship used.

steps: The co-interior (same-side interior) angle of the $124^\circ$ angle is supplementary to it: $180^\circ - 124^\circ = 56^\circ$ (co-interior angles between parallel lines are supplementary).
So one angle of the triangle is $56^\circ$ and a second is $46^\circ$.
By the triangle angle-sum theorem, the third angle is $180^\circ - 56^\circ - 46^\circ = 78^\circ$.
The third angle measures $78^\circ$.

items.prompt: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One angle is $(7x - 4)^\circ$ and a same-side interior (co-interior) angle is $(2x + 13)^\circ$. After solving for $x$, a second transversal forms a triangle that includes the $(7x - 4)^\circ$ angle as one of its interior angles together with a $40^\circ$ angle. Find the third angle of that triangle.
items.answer: $x = 19$; the third angle of the triangle is $11^\circ$

steps: Same-side interior (co-interior) angles between parallel lines are supplementary: $(7x - 4) + (2x + 13) = 180$.
Combine like terms: $9x + 9 = 180$.
Subtract $9$: $9x = 171$, so $x = 19$.
Evaluate the angle: $7(19) - 4 = 133 - 4 = 129^\circ$.
This $129^\circ$ angle and a $40^\circ$ angle are two angles of the triangle, so the third angle is $180^\circ - 129^\circ - 40^\circ = 11^\circ$ (triangle angle-sum theorem).

items.prompt: Triangles $ABC$ and $XYZ$ are similar, with the correspondence $A \leftrightarrow X$, $B \leftrightarrow Y$, $C \leftrightarrow Z$. In triangle $ABC$, angle $A = (4x + 5)^\circ$ and angle $B = 71^\circ$. In triangle $XYZ$, angle $X = 49^\circ$ and angle $Z = (5x + 5)^\circ$. Find $x$, then find every angle of both triangles.

steps: Corresponding angles of similar triangles are congruent, so angle $A$ equals angle $X$: $4x + 5 = 49$.
Subtract $5$: $4x = 44$, so $x = 11$.
Then angle $A = 4(11) + 5 = 49^\circ$, matching angle $X = 49^\circ$.
In triangle $ABC$, angle $C = 180^\circ - 49^\circ - 71^\circ = 60^\circ$ (triangle angle-sum theorem).
Because $C \leftrightarrow Z$, angle $Z = 60^\circ$; check the expression: $5(11) + 5 = 55 + 5 = 60^\circ$, which agrees.
By the similarity correspondence, angle $Y = $ angle $B = 71^\circ$. So both triangles have angles $49^\circ, 71^\circ, 60^\circ$, consistent with AA similarity.

items.prompt: In a figure, lines $\ell$ and $m$ are parallel. A transversal makes an angle of $(9x - 11)^\circ$ with $\ell$, and the vertical angle to its corresponding angle at $m$ is $(6x + 25)^\circ$. Find $x$ and the common angle measure.

steps: A corresponding angle at $m$ is congruent to the $(9x - 11)^\circ$ angle at $\ell$ (corresponding angles between parallel lines are congruent).
The vertical angle to that corresponding angle is also congruent to it (vertical angles are congruent), so the marked $(6x + 25)^\circ$ equals $(9x - 11)^\circ$.
Set the expressions equal: $9x - 11 = 6x + 25$.
Substitute: $9(12) - 11 = 108 - 11 = 97^\circ$ and $6(12) + 25 = 72 + 25 = 97^\circ$. The common measure is $97^\circ$.

items.prompt: In triangle $ABC$, side $AB$ is extended past $B$ to a point $D$. The exterior angle $CBD$ measures $(5x + 8)^\circ$. The two remote interior angles are $A = (3x - 2)^\circ$ and $C = (x + 30)^\circ$. Find $x$, then find the interior angle $ABC$.

steps: By the exterior-angle theorem, the exterior angle $CBD$ equals the sum of the two remote interior angles $A$ and $C$: $5x + 8 = (3x - 2) + (x + 30)$.
Combine like terms on the right: $5x + 8 = 4x + 28$.
Subtract $4x$ from both sides: $x + 8 = 28$.
Subtract $8$: $x = 20$.
The exterior angle is $5(20) + 8 = 108^\circ$. The interior angle $ABC$ is its linear-pair supplement: angle $ABC = 180^\circ - 108^\circ = 72^\circ$.

Check with the remote interiors: $A = 3(20) - 2 = 58^\circ$, $C = 20 + 30 = 50^\circ$, and $58^\circ + 50^\circ = 108^\circ$ equals the exterior angle; also $58^\circ + 50^\circ + 72^\circ = 180^\circ$.

items.prompt: A transversal crosses parallel lines $\ell$ and $m$, creating an alternate interior angle of $52^\circ$ at the lower line. That $52^\circ$ angle is one base angle of an isosceles triangle whose two base angles are equal. Find the vertex (apex) angle of the isosceles triangle, naming each relationship used.

steps: The base angle equals the given alternate interior angle, $52^\circ$ (alternate interior angles between parallel lines are congruent).
An isosceles triangle has two equal base angles, so both base angles measure $52^\circ$.
By the triangle angle-sum theorem, the apex angle is $180^\circ - 52^\circ - 52^\circ = 180^\circ - 104^\circ = 76^\circ$.
The vertex angle measures $76^\circ$.

items.prompt: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. A triangle is formed whose two angles on one side are an alternate interior angle of $(2x + 15)^\circ$ and an interior angle of $(4x + 12)^\circ$. The exterior angle of this triangle at its third vertex is $(7x + 9)^\circ$. Find $x$ and the measure of that exterior angle.

steps: The alternate interior angle keeps its given measure $(2x + 15)^\circ$ (alternate interior angles between parallel lines are congruent), so the two remote interior angles of the triangle are $(2x + 15)^\circ$ and $(4x + 12)^\circ$.
By the exterior-angle theorem, the exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles: $(2x + 15) + (4x + 12) = 7x + 9$.
Combine like terms on the left: $6x + 27 = 7x + 9$.
Subtract $6x$ from both sides: $27 = x + 9$. Subtract $9$: $x = 18$.
The exterior angle is $7(18) + 9 = 126 + 9 = 135^\circ$.
Check: the remote interiors are $2(18) + 15 = 51^\circ$ and $4(18) + 12 = 84^\circ$, and $51^\circ + 84^\circ = 135^\circ$, which matches the exterior angle.
